messages:
support-agent: FYI customer Acme-pay opened a support case — their Go app using the Redwood Go SDK gets a short stream then the connection appears to close. Happening on lots of requests, intermittently. They attached logs.

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro they used? suspect scanning/parsing issue on client side.

maria: They sent this snippet:```go
r, _ := client.Stream(ctx, req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
for scanner.Scan() {
  fmt.Println(scanner.Text())
}
```

alex: Yep, there's an obvious smell: Scanner splits on newlines and has a 64kb token limit by default. Chunked JSON streams that send long partial frames or no newline can get truncated. Scanner will return false and discard remainder when token too large.

josh: They claimed the server only sends short JSON deltas, but their logs show a single chunk with ~120kb of payload. Also they run through an Nginx reverse proxy which might be coalescing frames.

support-agent: Attaching a shortened snippet from their tcpdump: "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n...\r\n\n7b0\r\n{\"delta\":...120kb...}\r\n0\r\n\r\n"

maria: Reproduced locally by proxying via nginx with default buffering — nginx will buffer and release bigger chunks to the client. If client code expects line-delimited objects it can break.

alex: Two-pronged guidance: 1) stop using bufio.NewScanner for streaming JSON; 2) upgrade to the latest Go SDK — we changed server framing in v0.10 to be stable with json.Decoder reads and added content-type hints.

alex: Example recommended read pattern:```go
dec := json.NewDecoder(r)
for {
  var msg map[string]interface{}
  if err := dec.Decode(&msg); err == io.EOF {
    break
  } else if err != nil {
    log.Printf("decode err: %v", err)
    break
  }
  // handle msg
  fmt.Printf("MSG: %#v\n", msg)
}
```

josh: Alternative if messages are newline-delimited: use `bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n')` which doesn't have the token-size limit.

dev-bot: Note: customer reported Go SDK version 0.9.1. Changelog shows framing fixes in 0.10.0 and a streaming API tweak to expose a Reader directly.

support-agent: Action items for support: ask Acme-pay to try: 1) upgrade SDK to >= 0.10.0, 2) replace Scanner code with json.Decoder or ReadBytes, 3) if behind nginx/set `proxy_buffering off;` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to avoid re-chunking, 4) capture raw tcpdump if problem persists.

maria: Also call out retry interaction: they had a retry middleware that closed the response reader early and retried the request. If the app cancels / retries while consumer is still reading, you can get half frames. Recommend ensure consumer drains stream or set retry to 0 for streaming endpoints.

josh: Sharing a short repro we used:```bash
# emulate large single chunk
echo -e "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n1f4\r\n$(python3 -c 'print("{" + "\"delta\":\"x\"*80000 + "}\"")')\r\n0\r\n\r\n" | nc -l 18080
```

support-agent: Customer tried the decoder approach and reported the stream now stays open and receives full payloads. They will test behind their real infra tomorrow.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2025-342 streaming truncation (customer-facing). Assigned to alex.

support-agent: I'll follow up after they validate. If they still see issues we'll ask for raw tcpdump and nginx config. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
